Landing.heroLead: Heirloom encrypts your most important files in your browser and splits the key between guardians you choose. Nobody can open them early, not us, and not any single guardian.
Landing.heroNote: Runs on public testnets today. Needs a browser wallet such as MetaMask.
Landing.heroAria: A key split into three shares held by three guardians; two of three are enough to open the vault
Landing.problemTitle: The usual choices are a lawyer who holds everything, or a password in an envelope.
Landing.problemBody: The first asks you to trust one person with all of it. The second works until the envelope is lost, read, or forgotten. Heirloom replaces both with rules that are public, enforced by a contract, and decided by several people at once.
Landing.howTitle: Four steps, and no one in the middle.

s1.title: Seal
s1.body: Pick a file. Your browser encrypts it with a fresh key before anything leaves your device. Only scrambled bytes are ever uploaded.

s2.title: Split
s2.body: That key is cut into shares, one per guardian you trust, each locked to that guardian's own public key. Any two or more together can rebuild it. One alone learns nothing.

s3.title: Prove
s3.body: When you are gone, your beneficiary raises a claim with a certificate. Guardians open the evidence themselves and decide. The rules run on a public contract, not on our say-so.

s4.title: Release
s4.body: If enough guardians agree and you stay silent through the waiting period, they hand their shares to the beneficiary, who decrypts the file and checks it matches the original, byte for byte.

Landing.privTitle: What the world can see, and what never leaves you.

p1.b: A pointer to scrambled bytes on IPFS

p2.b: Their addresses, no names or documents

p3.b: A fingerprint of the evidence, never the evidence

p4.b: Timestamped on a public ledger anyone can audit

p1.b: Encrypted in the browser. Plaintext never reaches a server

p2.b: Sealed with your password, stored only on your device

p3.b: Exists whole only on your device and, later, the beneficiary's

p4.b: Encrypted for your guardians. We cannot read it

Landing.safeTitle: Built so a mistake can be undone, and a theft cannot hurry.

heartbeat.d: Check in with one tap. Any check-in after a claim is raised voids that claim, so a mistaken or malicious one dies on its own.

challenge.d: A waiting window you set, at least five minutes, in which you can object before anything is finalized.

fraud.d: Any guardian can flag a claim as fraudulent. It is blocked for good until you clear it yourself.

freeze.d: One button stops every claim on your vault. Unfreezing counts as a check-in.

timelock.d: Keep a file sealed until a date you choose, no matter how many guardians agree.

verified.d: Optionally require guardians to prove they are real, distinct people, and beneficiaries to prove who they are and that they are adults, using zero-knowledge proofs of Aadhaar. Nothing from the Aadhaar leaves the browser.

silent.d: If a guardian never answers, the claim can still finish after your deadline, as long as the minimum threshold approved.

Landing.rolesEyebrow: Three roles, one address can hold several

owner.p3: Check in, cancel, or freeze at any time

guardian.line: People you trust, none of them alone.
guardian.p1: Review the evidence in their own browser
guardian.p3: Release their share only after finalization

beneficiary.p1: Sees that a file exists, never what it holds
beneficiary.p2: Raises a claim once you have been silent long enough
beneficiary.p3: Decrypts only when guardians have released

Landing.ctaTitle: Start with one file. Choose who it is for.
Landing.footerNote: A working prototype on public testnets. Not audited. Do not store anything you cannot afford to lose.
